subject: On‑site cluster connectivity, egress profiles & persistent layer plan
messages:

Subject: Re: Private cluster planning — connectivity + storage overview

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the quick sync yesterday. We're starting to pull together the on‑prem intake packet for Site 7 (substation facility). Primary asks from my team:

- Clear recommended egress patterns for telemetry vs customer traffic (we need to control egress to our security appliances).
- Ingress/topology — we plan to run an internal load balancer and a separate external LB; want to understand how Redwood recommends handling kube‑mesh egress/NAT in a constrained CIDR.
- Persistent volumes: which classes do you recommend for KV cache (low‑latency) vs model artifacts (large, replicated blockstore)? Recovery SLA and snapshot cadence guidance would help.

Attached is a short site inventory (GG-site‑inventory-brief.pdf). Can we get a short written approach so our ops lead can validate with networking/security?

Thanks — happy to jump on a call.

—Matt

Matt — thanks for the inventory and the clear asks.

High level we can turn this into a two‑page operational approach and a short runbook for the on‑site handoff. Quick answers up front:

1) Egress profiles: we recommend three egress classes — telemetry (TLS to our ingest endpoints), customer‑facing (external LB), and control plane (private, VPC only). Each class maps to a specific NAT path and ACLs on your edge firewall.

2) Kube‑mesh: we prefer a cilium dataplane with eBPF for Site 7 due to its lighter netfilter overhead and clearer egress policy primitives. We will provide network policy templates for split egress.

3) PV guidance: KV cache on local NVMe (fast ephemeral with scheduled warmup and daily snapshot to the blockstore); model artifacts on replicated blockstore (NFS or iSCSI backed) with hourly integrity checks and daily incremental snapshots.

I asked Marissa to draft the egress matrix and PV class options (attached). Jordan will confirm the node taints/eviction strategy for mixed NVMe + blockstore fleets.

Next steps: Marissa and Jordan + I will finalize the short doc and share a draft by EOD. Proposed on‑site review (ops + networking + security): Tue 2028‑08‑02. Does that work?

Thanks,

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 Jul 2028 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private cluster planning — connectivity + storage overview

Neha/Jordan — draft notes from my side (quick scan, not exhaustive):

- Egress matrix (see sheet): map flows to three paths and required ACLs. Key item: telemetry egress must be allowed only to specific FQDNs/IPs and use mTLS from the node agent. Use a dedicated SNAT gateway for telemetry so we can assert identity upstream.

- Ingress patterns: external LB -> dedicated external nodepool (no access to internal blockstore), internal LB -> internal nodepool behind a service mesh gateway. Avoid hairpin NAT by keeping external LB outside the cluster network and injecting service routes in the border router.

- Kube‑mesh: Cilium (v1.15+) with egress policies and eBPF redirect for policy enforcement. If security insists on iptables-based auditing we can fall back to Calico but note throughput penalty on high connection churn.

- Nodepool sizing: suggest three nodepools — control (smaller, t3‑like vCPU profile), worker‑external (high NIC bandwidth, GPU if needed), worker‑internal (fast NVMe for cache + local SSD). Use taints: nodepool=external:NoSchedule / nodepool=internal:NoSchedule and tolerations on workloads.

- PV classes:
  * fast-local-nvme (localPersistentVolume + retention script) — use for KV cache, set reclaimPolicy: Retain and daily snapshot to replicated blockstore.
  * replicated-blockstore (iSCSI) — for model artifacts, multi‑attach supported, replicate across two controllers inside site.
  * archive-s3 (object gateway on premise) — for older artifacts, lifecycle 30d -> cold.

- Eviction: aggressive QoS for cache pods (Burstable + limits) and a preStop hook that ensures graceful flush to NVMe. If disk pressure occurs, prefer eviction from external worker pool first.

I'll attach the egress matrix and PV proposals. We should also include a small iptables/nft ruleset the site firewall team can import.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 Jul 2028 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private cluster planning — connectivity + storage overview

Folks — a few clarifications from infra/ops perspective before we send to GreenGrid: 

On the NVMe + blockstore split: fully agree with local NVMe for KV cache but we need a concrete snapshot/restore plan that tolerates power losses at the site. Proposal:
- Use LVM snapshots to flush KV cache to a small persistent LVM volume, then rsync to replicated blockstore; if rsync fails mark node for quarantine and rely on warm cache fallback.
- Retention: keep 7 daily snapshots and one weekly; store manifests in the replicated store to allow restore.

On NAT and egress: confirm whether the site firewall can present multiple SNAT pools; if not we will multiplex telemetry over dedicated port ranges and use mTLS cert pinning to differentiate traffic. That will increase load on the SNAT gateway — recommend a single HA pair with health probes.

Taints/tolerations: add a soft taint on external pool (preferNoSchedule) so scheduled maintenance can preempt noncritical customer traffic first.

I'll add a small appendix to the runbook describing failure scenarios and the recommended automated playbooks (drain + snapshot + failover).

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Engineering Manager, Deployment Services
jordan.blake@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Private cluster planning — connectivity + storage overview

Matt — attaching the consolidated runbook draft and our proposed on‑site review agenda. Summary / decisions for your team to validate:

- Egress: three logical classes (telemetry SNAT pair; customer external; control plane). If site cannot provide multiple SNAT pools we will multiplex and use mTLS identification.
- Mesh: Cilium recommended; fallback to Calico if auditing requires it.
- Storage: KV cache on local NVMe with daily snapshot to replicated blockstore; model artifacts on replicated blockstore with hourly checks. Retention: 7 daily + weekly snapshot manifests.
- Nodepools & taints: control / worker‑external / worker‑internal with recommended taints/tolerations and a preferNoSchedule on external pool for maintenance tolerance.
- On‑site review proposed: Tue 2028‑08‑02 at 10:00am PT (ops + networking + security).

Next steps: sign off on the two choices below and we'll lock the runbook for the on‑site review:
A) Accept Cilium path + NVMe snapshot plan (fast recovery, slightly more complex local scripts)
B) Require iptables auditing -> Calico fallback + simpler egress NAT (throughput hit on busy flows)

Please reply with A or B and any compliance constraints we should fold in. I've shared the doc here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cGG-runbook and attached the draft runbook and matrices.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Architect — Private Deployments
